main_text.p: fes, Iones, Perrhæbos, Magnetes, Locren-fes, Oetæos, Phthios, Maleenses, Phocen-ses: & harum gentium unamquamq; demonstrabam par suffragii jus habere, maximam idem quod minimam: eum, qui venisset Dorio, & Cytinio, tantum valere, quantum Lacedæmonios. Binum enim quamlibet gentem suffragium ferre. Ex Ionibus item Erythraum & Prienensem, quantum Athenienses: ac cæteros eodem modo. Porrò, Amphictyones præter munus id, quod jam expositum, curam templi Delphici & anathematum ac thesaurorum ejus, qui maximi erant, demandatam habuêre, eorumque defensores fuêre, multa quoq; anathemata ipsi in templo posuêre. Ad hæc ludos Pythios in honorem Apollinis, commissis primum cantoribus inter se certantibus, dein & aliis, lustà, cursu omnis generis contendentibus, instituerunt, & iis altero quoque anno præfederunt.

At enim non parva mutatio facta in hac curiâ Amphictyonicâ tempore Philippi Macedonis, qui pater Alexandri Magni fuit. Nam is bello sacro victor Phocenses ob sacrilegium commissum, Lacedæmonios ob adjutos sacrilegos Phocenses jure illo exuit, & id Macedo-niæ suæ contribuit, ut Pausanias docet. Verum post annos circiter LXVIII

page.notes: Printed text is set in long s (s), normalised to plain s. Lowercase "s" in "Iones" and "Pausanias" was read as the printed forms. "lustà" and "præfederunt" are read from the scan and not certain; "LXVIII" at the line end is partly cut off by the edge and may be read wrongly. The mark at the foot left ("+ ‡") is not clearly a signature and is left out. No margin notes are printed on this page. The left edge is dark because of the book's edge and was not transcribed.
